correctness.rationale: The entire derivation space is D(a,b,c) with diagonal entries (a,2a,3a) and subdiagonal entries (b,b,c); the automorphisms are G(h,t,u)=[[h,0,0],[t,h²,0],[u,ht,h³]], h!=0. Matrix conjugation yields a fixed, b→hb−at/h, c→h²c+a(t/h)^2−2au/h. For a!=0 and odd q, t kills b and u kills c; in char 2, after killing b the invariant Δ=ac+b² is zero or nonzero, all nonzero squares being equivalent in F_{2^s}. For a=0,b!=0, c/b² classifies, giving q orbits size q−1. For a=b=0, square-class quotient of c gives two odd-characteristic or one even-characteristic orbit; zero singleton. Sums reproduce q³, including q=2 and3. Source matrix finite-field verifier enumerates q={2,3,4,5,7,8,9}; all-field proof uses no invalid division by 2 in characteristic 2.

value.rationale: The finite-field conjugacy quotient of infinitesimal symmetries is a natural classification invariant, and characteristic-two splitting into Δ=0/nonzero produces genuinely different moduli and orbit statistics not supplied merely by the two standard matrix tables.

final_claim: For the 3D left null-filiform Leibniz algebra [e1,e1]=e2,[e1,e2]=e3 over every F_q, the quotient of its ordinary derivations under automorphism conjugacy has exactly 2q+2 orbits for odd q and 3q for even q; explicit representatives and orbit sizes follow from the complete conjugation action, with nonzero a in characteristic two split by ac+b^2=0.
limitations: The finite checks do not establish the formula for all prime-power q; source algebraic proof does.
